headline: SLAM EXPLORATION DISCOVERS NEW Cu-Ni-Co ZONE AT GOODWIN — 67.4m SULPHIDE 2km NORTHWEST OF LOGAN TARGET, BATHURST CAMP NB
snippet: SLAM Exploration (TSXV: SXL) disclosed a new mineral discovery from drill hole GW26-36 at the Goodwin copper-nickel-cobalt project in the Bathurst Mining Camp, New Brunswick: the hole intersected 67.4 metres of sustained pyrrhotite-chalcopyrite sulphide mineralization from 124.4 to 191.8 metres depth, located 2,000 metres northwest of the known Logan zone and coincident with a VTEM geophysical plate model. Companion holes GW26-37 and GW26-38 also intersected sulphide mineralization, confirming the discovery's lateral extent across three consecutive holes — assays from 992 submitted core samples are pending, and drilling resumes next week to complete the 2026 campaign.

headline: SILVER HOLDS ABOVE $69 WITH 17% AUGUST GAIN AND 77% YEAR-OVER-YEAR SURGE — SIXTH STRAIGHT PHYSICAL SUPPLY DEFICIT COMPOUNDS INDUSTRIAL DEMAND
snippet: Silver is trading at $69.34 per ounce on August 27, up 1.82% on the day and holding a 17–18% month-over-month gain that makes August its strongest calendar month in over a year — the metal is up 77% year-over-year as the market runs its sixth consecutive structural physical supply deficit while industrial consumption accelerates from AI data center infrastructure, solar photovoltaics, and EV systems. Primary silver miners leveraged to the spot price have broadly outperformed both gold equities and the wider market through August, with the gold-silver ratio compressing from recent highs as silver catches up to gold's earlier move.

headline: NUCLEAR STOCKS UP 16% IN AUGUST — UEC +38%, ENERGY FUELS +39%, DENISON +33% AS U3O8 SPOT NEARS $90/LB 6-MONTH HIGH
snippet: The VanEck Uranium and Nuclear ETF gained 16% in August — its best monthly performance since January — led by Energy Fuels Inc. (+39%), Uranium Energy Corp. (+38%), and Denison Mines (+33%), even as U3O8 spot rose only modestly to near $90 per pound. Analysts attribute the re-rating to three converging catalysts: delays at Kazatomprom's TQZ sulphuric acid plant reducing Kazakhstan's near-term output, technology giants signing new nuclear capacity agreements for AI data centers, and growing conviction that the uranium market is structurally undersupplied through the decade of reactor construction commitments ahead.

headline: CANSTAR HITS WIDEST SULPHIDE IN MARY MARCH HISTORY — 15.6m AT 2.3% CuEq INCLUDING 9.75m AT 3.3% CuEq, VMS SYSTEM OPEN IN ALL DIRECTIONS
snippet: Canstar Resources (TSXV: ROX) reported the widest massive sulphide intercept in the Mary March Project's drilling history from its 2026 summer program in Newfoundland: hole MM-26-42 intersected 15.6 metres grading 2.3% copper equivalent at 467 metres downhole, including 9.75 metres at 3.3% CuEq, hosted in the fault-bounded Fleetway Rhyolite flow-dome. The full width was not intersected, the mineralization remains open along strike and at depth, and all four holes of the 2026 summer drill program intersected VMS-style mineralization, confirming the system's continuity.

headline: LAKE VICTORIA GOLD HITS 28.71 g/t AU FROM 21m DEPTH AT IMWELO — NEAR-SURFACE HIGH GRADE ANCHORS OPEN-PIT MINE PLAN IN TANZANIA
snippet: Lake Victoria Gold (TSXV: LVG) reported high-grade results from near-surface HQ diamond drilling at its Imwelo Gold Project in Tanzania: hole IMWDR029 returned 28.71 g/t gold over 2.75 metres from just 21 metres depth, while hole IMWDR028 intersected 12.20 g/t Au over 4.50 metres from 32 metres — with individual quartz-vein samples grading up to 142.90 g/t Au. The intercepts occur within the shallow weathered sequence at Area C, Imwelo's planned initial open-pit mining area, and feed grade-control data directly into detailed mine planning for a project sandwiched between two of Tanzania's largest producing gold mines.

headline: CABRAL GOLD INTERSECTS NEW ZONE 200m SOUTH OF MAIN BODY AT JERIMUM CIMA — 8.9m AT 5.8 g/t AU INCLUDING 28.4 g/t HIGHLIGHT IN BRAZIL
snippet: Cabral Gold (TSXV: CBR) reported that hole DDH411 at the Jerimum Cima target in Brazil's Cuiú Cuiú Gold District intersected 8.9 metres grading 5.8 g/t gold from 208.1 metres, including 1.8 metres at 28.4 g/t — interpreted as a new mineralized zone located 200 metres south of the main Jerimum Cima body, trending east-west parallel to the main zone and open to the east, west, and at depth. The new zone meaningfully expands Cuiú Cuiú's resource potential and adds a second target thread to the district alongside the main zone that Cabral is advancing toward a resource estimate.

headline: COPPER GIANT DRILLS 771m AT 0.54% CuEq AT PORPHYRY TARGET — Cu-Mo MINERALIZATION EXTENDS SOUTHEAST AND AT DEPTH
snippet: Copper Giant Resources (TSXV: CGNT) intersected 771 metres grading 0.54% copper equivalent (0.33% Cu and 0.039% Mo) in its latest drill hole, extending the copper-molybdenum porphyry mineralization both to the southeast and at depth — a result that indicates the system is growing in two directions and may support a meaningful increase in the known footprint. In the context of copper trading near $6.57 per pound after its August surge to all-time highs, bulk-tonnage porphyry copper drill results are drawing renewed attention from investors repositioning into copper exposure ahead of a structural supply deficit that analysts see persisting through the decade.

headline: HOTTER PCE PULLS GOLD BACK TO $4,633 — 3.7% JULY INFLATION PRINT LIFTS YIELDS AND TRIMS RATE-HOLD ODDS AHEAD OF WARSH KEYNOTE
snippet: July PCE inflation registered 3.7% year-over-year — above the 3.6% consensus forecast — sending Treasury yields higher and pulling spot gold back 0.52% to $4,633.50 on August 26 as traders trimmed long positions ahead of Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote Friday. Markets now price a 60% probability of no September rate change, down from 64% pre-data; the tighter path for gold adds two-way risk into one of the most consequential Fed speeches of 2026, with structurally bullish analysts arguing any hawkish surprise is a buying opportunity rather than a trend reversal.

headline: KITCO GOLD SWOT: U.S. DEBT BUYBACK SURPRISE DRIVES DOLLAR LOWER AND GOLD TO $4,625 — STRATEGISTS REVIVE $5,000 YEAR-END TARGET
snippet: Kitco's weekly Gold SWOT analysis frames gold's August surge as primarily debt-driven: the U.S. Treasury's surprise announcement of ramped-up long-dated debt buybacks sent the dollar sharply lower and gold up 2.4% to $4,625 in a single session, prompting multiple strategists to revive $5,000 per ounce year-end targets. The column flags rising mine-cost guidance as the sector's central risk, cautioning that producers with a history of cost overruns could see multiple compression even as bullion breaks higher — widening the performance gap between the commodity and the equities.

headline: 13 OF 19 RARE EARTH ELEMENTS FELL IN AUGUST — BASKET DROPS 11.9% AS CHINA DELAYS H2 MINING QUOTA, GALLIUM LEADS DECLINES AT -18.8%
snippet: The rare earth market posted a broad August pullback with 13 of 19 tracked elements declining — average monthly change -5.4%, median -9.2% — dropping the basket 11.9% from July's $110.55/kg reading and pushing it below the $110/kg DoD-backed price floor for the first time. Gallium led declines at -18.8% while the NdPr magnet-metal complex was essentially flat; China's MIIT H2 mining and smelting quota, the single largest open catalyst for the sector, remained unpublished as of the August update, and the price gap between Chinese domestic terbium and ex-China transactions remained extreme near $5,000 per kilogram outside China.
